summary: 1952 steel fire tower with a 14-foot metal cab on the Talimena Scenic Highway; used for fire detection until 1975, now an observation tower. Heights disagree.

facts.design: Cl-100 metal cab on a steel tower

access.note: Observation tower beside the Talimena Scenic Highway, with a Forest Service placard at the site

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Ouachita National Forest

events.note: Register and Encyclopedia of Arkansas both give 1952; a hiking group page gives 1954 (see notes)
Disputed: a hiking group page dates the 14 by 14 foot cab to 1954; the register and Encyclopedia say 1952

evidence.supports: at the highest point of the Talimena Scenic Highway; picnic spot
evidence.quote: Rich Mountain Fire Tower is at the highest point on the road and is a popular picnic spot.

evidence.supports: Ouachita National Forest, Polk County, Arkansas
evidence.quote: Ouachita National Forest Polk County, Arkansas

evidence.supports: 42 ft steel tower, 14x14 Cl-100 metal cab, built 1952, fire detection until 1975
evidence.quote: The 42’ steel tower with a 14’x14’ Cl-100 metal cab was constructed in 1952 and used for fire detection until 1975.

evidence.supports: replaced an unusual wooden cab on a 20 ft log tower
evidence.quote: It replaced an unusual 6’x6’ wooden cab perched atop a 20’ log tower

evidence.supports: 58 ft observation tower built 1952; fire detection until 1975
evidence.quote: At the apex of Rich Mountain is a fifty-eight-foot observation tower constructed in 1952 and used for fire detection and prevention until 1975.

evidence.supports: replaced an unusual wooden cab on a twenty-foot log tower
evidence.quote: It was reported to have replaced an unusual wooden cab perched atop a twenty-foot log tower

evidence.supports: Forest Service placard describes the family that lived in the tower
evidence.quote: Shown on a forest service placard at this location is a short description of the history of the family that originally lived in the tower

evidence.supports: hiking group page dates the cab to 1954, used until 1975
evidence.quote: was constructed in 1954 and used for fire detection until 1975.

evidence.supports: hiking group page gives 14 x 14 cab, 65 ft high
evidence.quote: it measured 14' x 14' and stood 65 ' high.

evidence.supports: earlier towers on the summit; wooden fire tower replaced a pine-tree platform in 1910
evidence.quote: The first observation tower on Rich Mountain consisted of a pine tree with a platform. It was replaced in 1910 with a wooden fire tower.

notes_for_editor: Height conflict left unresolved: 42 ft steel tower (register), 58 ft observation tower (Encyclopedia of Arkansas), 65 ft with a 14 by 14 cab (hiking group page). These may describe different structures or measuring points; not confirmed. Build year: 1952 (register, Encyclopedia) vs 1954 (hiking group page). Elevation: register 2,646 ft (807 m; the record's 806.5 m matches) vs Encyclopedia 2,681 ft. Current hours and climbing rules are not verified; a search snippet describes weekend hours from an older guide and was not used. The Central US Lookouts page was read, but the text returned was only an index, so it is not cited. The record already has a public-domain NARA photo on Wikimedia; no new photos.
